problem_html:
H-JEPA plans top-down. A level-2 world model, optimised by gradient descent over 800 candidate latent-action sequences, proposes the next latent subgoal. A level-1 model-predictive controller (MPC) then tries to reach that subgoal within 10 environment steps before the whole hierarchy replans. Nothing in this loop checks whether the subgoal is actually executable by the low-level controller under its horizon and search budget.

RASR adds three pieces on top of the frozen, pretrained H-JEPA:

  1. Reachability estimator R(zt, g, H, B): probability that the level-1 MPC with budget B reaches latent subgoal g from the current latent zt within H steps, trained on real MPC executions.
  2. Reachability-aware selection (P2): rerank the unchanged level-2 candidate pool by progress cost − λ·cmin·log(R + δ).
  3. Failure monitoring + local repair (P3): detect stalls from planner-visible signals, re-solve the subgoal with a reachability term (and a visited-region penalty), and fall back to full replanning when the repaired subgoal is still unreachable.

Research question: under the same evaluation tasks and comparable compute, does reachability + local repair beat plain H-JEPA, more frequent replanning, and full replanning on the same trigger?
mermaid:
flowchart LR
  O[current frame o_t] --> E[frozen H-JEPA encoders]
  G[goal frame] --> E
  E --> L2[level-2 GD planner 800 candidates]
  L2 -->|candidate subgoals + progress cost| P2[P2 rerank cost - λ log R]
  R[(reachability MLP R z,g,H,B)] --> P2
  P2 -->|subgoal g| L1[level-1 MPC 100 samples, 10 steps]
  L1 --> ENV[FourRoom env]
  ENV --> O
  ENV -.-> M{monitor subgoal misses / goal stall}
  M -->|trigger| RP[P3 repair GD with R + novelty terms]
  R --> RP
  RP -->|R below tau| FB[fallback: full replan]
  RP --> L1
  FB --> L1
setup_html:
• Code: official kevinghst/H-JEPA at commit 97054ec, unmodified. All RASR code wraps or subclasses upstream objects; with every RASR switch off the planner is bit-identical to upstream (regression test).
  • Environment: FourRoom Distractors (224×224 pixels, one moving distractor, agent speed 2.5 px/step, success = within 16 px of the goal, 210-step budget). Chosen over Visual AntMaze because it needs no MuJoCo rendering, has an env-native success signal and its state can be restored exactly for branching rollouts.
  • Model / planner: pretrained 2-level H-JEPA (seed 42) with the official fourroom_l2 planner: level-2 GD with 800 samples and a decaying horizon of 12; level-1 GD MPC with 100 samples, a horizon of 2 × 5-step action blocks, replanning every 10 steps.
  • Tasks and splits: test = the official 50 start–goal tasks (two-room crossings). Train (40) and val (20) task sets were generated with the official generator under different seeds (1001, 2002 vs. 3072), so no start–goal configuration is shared. Train is used to fit the reachability models; every threshold, temperature and λ is chosen on val.
  • Determinism: upstream resets FourRoom without a seed, and two runs of the official eval.py gave different step counts (168 vs 141 on task 0). We seed each reset (100000 + task) and enable deterministic torch kernels; runs are bit-reproducible across processes.
  • Privileged state: simulator xy is used only for labels' calibration, evaluation and the analysis-only latent→xy probe in figures. The planner sees pixels, latents, model predictions and the reachability model.
  • Hardware: one RTX 4090 shared by up to 7 jobs. Wall-clock numbers are therefore inflated; predictor call counts are the comparable compute measure.
p0_html:
The instrumented runner mirrors the upstream chunked evaluation (one world per task, planner generators reseeded to seed + task) and logs, per planning call: the latents of the current frame and goal, the level-1 subgoal, all predicted level-1/level-2 plans, horizons, gradient-descent iterations, predictor forward calls and wall-clock. Per step it logs xy, distractors, actions and the real-frame latents, plus an env snapshot before every planning call.

The seed-42 baseline reaches 86% (43/50), inside the paper's 81.3 ± 6.7% range. All 7 failures occur in tasks with every door open (7 of 14 such tasks fail; 36 of 36 tasks with a closed door succeed).
p1_html:
Attempt. Restore the env at a baseline planning call, freeze the level-2 subgoal g the baseline gave its level-1 MPC, and run only the frozen level-1 MPC towards g for 30 steps with budget B ∈ {B0 = 2 GD iterations × 4 samples, B1 = 10 × 20, B2 = 90 × 100 (baseline)}. Labels for H ∈ {5, 10, 20, 30} are prefixes of the same rollout. Label: Y = 1 iff mink≤H ‖enc2(ot+k) − g‖² ≤ ε, with ε = 6.70: the median latent distance between real frames whose agents are within 8 px (about 3 agent steps), computed on the train split only.

A restored branch reproduces the logged frame to within 1/255 per pixel. Branch-B2 labels agree with the baseline's own execution of the same subgoal for 84% (H = 10) of 500 matched calls; the rest is solver noise, so labels are partly stochastic.
p1_after_html: The distance-only logistic model already reaches 0.877 AUROC: most of the reachability signal is "how far is the subgoal, and how much budget and time does the controller get". The MLP adds a clear gain within each (H, B) cell (0.853 vs 0.751 for kNN and 0.731 for the reference), and after temperature scaling on val it is the best-calibrated model (ECE 0.022). Three MLP training seeds give test AUROC 0.870, 0.906 and 0.903.

source activate_rasr.sh
scripts/launch_p0.sh                          # P0 baseline, 50 official tasks
scripts/launch_p1_baselines.sh                # baseline on RASR train/val tasks (P1 source)
scripts/launch_p1_collect.sh                  # branch attempts
python scripts/train_reachability.py          # eps, kNN, MLP, metrics, calibration plots
scripts/launch_p2p3.sh val  rerank_l0.25 rerank_l0.5 rerank_l1.0 rasr_b5 rasr_b20 full_replan
scripts/launch_p2p3.sh test rerank_l0.25 full_replan rasr_b20 repair_noR
scripts/launch_b2_shards.sh 0-27 28-49        # B2: replan every 5 steps
python scripts/compare_methods.py ...         # tables in outputs/rasr/p2p3/
xargs -P 6 -L 1 scripts/run_seed_job.sh < outputs/rasr/p4_jobs.txt   # planner seeds 43, 44
python scripts/aggregate_seeds.py             # 3-seed table
scripts/launch_p4_shift.sh && python scripts/eval_shift.py   # predictor on non-selected candidates
python -m pytest -q tests/                    # unit + GPU regression tests
